competition.flat_book_pnl: A flat seat has zero net financing/competition P&L: paper NAV earning SOFR is benchmarked at SOFR, so those flows cancel, and shocked-risk financing is zero.
competition.funding_basis: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 is the zero-return competition benchmark, not free alpha. Every seat has $100m paper NAV that may be described as earning SOFR, but that capital is equally funded/benchmarked at SOFR so those flows cancel. Deployed shocked-risk capital pays the same official SOFR on trusted standard-shock risk capital: the absolute MTM loss from a 1% adverse spot move, a 100bp (1 percentage point) adverse outright rate move, or a 100bp adverse curve/RV spread move. Supported STIR contracts use exchange DV01 and currency conversion; historical rows without that stamp keep the legacy duration-one vintage and are not silently restated. Equal risk capital receives equal financing treatment across asset classes. Notional is descriptive, not the funding base. A completely flat book — including no-trade-skeptic — therefore has zero net financing/competition P&L from SOFR cash or funding economics. Positive financing/carry alpha requires an explicit markable strategy that earns above SOFR or funds below SOFR. Weekends and holidays carry the last applicable published fixing until the next fixing. If official fixing history cannot be established, new funding accrual fails closed and prior canonical balances are preserved.
competition.instruction: Do not optimize for gross notional or fill available capacity. Size risk from plausible adverse paths and historical excursions while staying inside the trusted risk-capital and drawdown limits. Flat cash at SOFR is the zero benchmark, not a source of alpha. The no-trade-skeptic must include a structured funding_view on every new risk or NO_TRADE thesis: the frozen official SOFR fixing, the relevant SR3 forward-curve view, its own assessment of whether realized funding will print higher, lower, or about the same as the curve, and the implication for remaining at the zero SOFR benchmark versus paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital.
competition.objective: Finish with the highest cumulative net paper P&L across the 14 standing seats.

research_supplement.summary: The dollar is breaking higher against the euro, sterling, the Australian dollar and the kiwi, while U.S. yields and the secured-funding strip are higher. The S&P 500 is 7323, gold is 3742, and crude is elevated but well off the prior spike, with WTI at 83.26 and Brent at 91.95. Fed minutes showed officials still open to more hikes and worried that AI could add to inflation, and Governor Waller talked about a possible half-point move. Treasury yields were inching higher into the morning after that session. The Bank of Japan governor remained open to tightening despite weak consumption. New Zealand's governor cited above-target inflation and an uneven recovery; sovereign yields there are unavailable, while kiwi spot is still a live price. Canada retail trade and Japan CPI are next, then Australian prices and U.S. growth data, ahead of the December central-bank decisions.

expression_memo.rationale: Flat. The dollar strip premium is the hike path, Aussie spot carry is being overwhelmed at 0.6731, and the Canadian front-end jump is still in motion.

carry-is-king.invalidation: The flat stance ends if a receiver or a higher-yielding currency shows a forward spread that is still a cushion once the hawkish path is treated as delivered, and if that spot is no longer breaking down.
carry-is-king.thesis: Nothing is put on. Receiving the secured-funding strip earns the gap over cash at 3.92 only if the priced hikes are not delivered, and the minutes say those hikes are the path. Australian spot carry is being overwhelmed by a breakdown at 0.6731. Canada's two-year jump of 17 basis points is a live repricing, not settled carry.

expression_memo.rationale: Flat. The hawkish catalyst has already repriced the dollar and the front end, and the next data prints do not have a signed gap left to trade.

catalyst-junkie.invalidation: The flat stance is wrong only if a later fact shows the half-point shock still unabsorbed with March secured funding still near 4.575, or if Japan, Canada, or Australia data print against a gap these marks do not contain.
catalyst-junkie.thesis: Nothing is booked. The minutes and the half-point remark are already in the price: euro has broken at 1.0968, the two-year is 4.80, and March secured funding at 4.575 sits well above cash at 3.92. Canada retail trade, Japan CPI, and the December central-bank meetings are on the calendar, and none of them has an unspent gap that these marks can size. Dollar-yen at 159.42 is two-way into a Bank of Japan that is open to a hike.

expression_memo.rationale: Flat. The upside breaks are extended and the downside breaks are late, and the missing adverse-close level would have to be invented.

chart-guy.invalidation: A later pass needs one 20-day break with RSI outside the 30 and 70 extension band and a visible adverse daily close. A further extension of the same stretched breaks does not by itself create the trade.
chart-guy.thesis: No new spot is taken. The confirmed breaks are real, but the upside names are already extended, with dollar-Canada and dollar-franc RSIs at 72 and 71, and the cleanest downside names are late, with euro RSI at 28.8 and the Australian dollar at 23.4. Dollar-yen is not a break, and Aussie-Canada has not confirmed one. Without a visible adverse close to define the stop, none of these is a 5-day or 20-day trade today.

expression_memo.rationale: Close the 8 million euro-sterling long. The isolated residual of the dollar break has broken, and no Europe policy wedge in the marks carries the long through it.

spot_candidate.rationale: Spot 0.8329 versus a 0.83305 entry is a 20-day downside break. The close removes the residual rather than replacing it with an unconfirmed Aussie-Canada short.

cross-merchant.invalidation: The exit is wrong if euro-sterling reclaims the pre-break 20-day range and euro stops underperforming sterling. A later confirmed break in Aussie-Canada could be the next cross, and it is not this one.
cross-merchant.thesis: Euro-sterling is closed. The cross is the residual of a joint euro and sterling breakdown, and that residual has itself broken, with spot 0.8329, a 20-day downside break, and a one-year percentile of 0.2. Sterling is the firmer European leg. Aussie-Canada is not a cleaner replacement: the break is unconfirmed and the short would pay the Australia-versus-Canada carry.

expression_memo.rationale: Hold the 10 million euro short. Spot 1.0968 versus a 1.1081 entry is a live 20-day downside break, and the hawkish minutes still support the dollar leg.

spot_candidate.rationale: Euro at 1.0968 is the clean dollar short. RSI 28.8 argues against adding, not against keeping the break.

harvest_review.remaining_edge_reason: Euro at 1.0968 is still the live 20-day downside break, and a fresh short at this level would still be the clean dollar expression of the hawkish minutes. The hot RSI bars an add, not the existing 10 million.

reunderwrite.catalyst_logic: The hawkish minutes are the catalyst. A reclaim of the broken range would exhaust it.
reunderwrite.realization_logic: The short pays if the 20-day downside break extends while the two-year stays near 4.80.

expression_memo.rationale: Hold the 10 million dollar-franc long. Spot 0.8427 versus a 0.8393 entry is a 20-day upside break. Gold and a 25 vol reading are reasons not to add, not reasons to exit while the break holds.

spot_candidate.rationale: Dollar-franc is the dollar against a low-yielder, distinct from the euro short only while 0.8427 holds the upside break.

harvest_review.remaining_edge_reason: Dollar-franc at 0.8427 is still the 20-day upside break against a low-yielder. A fresh long at this level would still express the dollar bid, and the gold and vol readings only bar an add.

reunderwrite.catalyst_logic: A loss of the upside break, or a safe-haven spike that reverses 0.8427 through 0.8393, exhausts the edge.
reunderwrite.realization_logic: The long pays if the upside break holds and the dollar bid from the minutes persists.

dollar-king.invalidation: The euro short comes off if euro reclaims the broken 20-day range or trades back through 1.1081. The franc long comes off if dollar-franc loses the upside break or trades back through 0.8393.

causal.assumptions_right: Elevated U.S. yields did keep the dollar supported against the yen from 158.06 through 159.42. Verbal openness to a hike was not itself a hike, and the tape did not reverse on a policy event.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The exit treated openness to a hike as if it were the written invalidation. That underweighted the gap between a speech and a move in Japanese funding, and it used intervention as a reason to flatten without an intervention print.
causal.causal_divergence: The chain from a wide funding gap to a higher dollar-yen was still in force at 159.30. The position was removed by the timing of the flatten, not by the stop.
causal.future_implication: Dollar-yen stays off until a real policy, funding, or intervention event, or until a fresh breakout appears that the euro short and the franc long do not already express.
causal.observed_reality: The position was closed at 159.30. The next marks show 159.42, still not a breakout, the two-year at 4.80, and only an openness to a hike rather than a delivered one.
causal.original_belief: The long at 158.06 was meant to stay on while U.S. funding stayed restrictive and until the Bank of Japan actually hiked, funding converged, or intervention appeared.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: On the information at the exit, the rule was to keep the long until a hike, a funding convergence, or intervention printed. The next mark at 159.42 was a non-breakout, which argues for a smaller residual with the same stop, not for a new add.

postmortems.future_rule: Keep a dollar-yen long until one of those three events prints. Do not reopen dollar-yen while the dollar length is already in the euro short and the franc long and the pair is not breaking out.
postmortems.lesson: Do not close a dollar-yen long on hike rhetoric. The invalidation is a delivered hike with Japanese funding catching up, dollar funding converging, or intervention.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: The rate-gap thesis was intact at the exit. The tactical case for staying long was thinner than the structural gap because dollar-yen had stopped breaking out, but the written stop had not printed.
postmortems.what_failed: The long was closed before a delivered Bank of Japan hike, a funding convergence, or intervention. A governor who is open to a hike is not that invalidation, and 159.42 is still not a 20-day breakout.
postmortems.what_worked: The dollar-yen long from 158.06 tracked a still-wide dollar funding gap. Spot was 159.30 at the exit and is 159.42 now, with the two-year at 4.80.

dollar-king.thesis: The euro short and the dollar-franc long stay on. Euro at 1.0968 is still through the 20-day low, and dollar-franc at 0.8427 is still through the 20-day high, with the two-year at 4.80 after a hawkish set of minutes. Dollar-yen at 159.42 is not a breakout, and dollar-Canada is an oil-linked extra rather than a third dollar ticket. Nothing is added.

expression_memo.rationale: Close the 10 million dollar-yen short. It is the wrong residual, and the stretched dollar breaks are not yet reversible.

spot_candidate.rationale: Spot 159.42 versus a 159.60 entry is only a small gain, and a one-year z-score of 0.52 is not a fade. Euro at 1.0968 is the larger stretch and is not opened without a reversal condition.

mean-reverter.invalidation: A later fade needs a named reversal, such as a failed break or a rejection close, on one of the stretched markets. The yen short is not kept as a substitute for that missing condition.
mean-reverter.thesis: The dollar-yen short is closed. It is a small gain from 159.60 to 159.42, and it is not the stretch: the one-year z-score is 0.52 and RSI is 59. The stretches are euro, dollar-franc, dollar-Canada, and euro-sterling, and each of those is a fresh break. A break that started this week is not a reversal condition, so none of them is faded.

expression_memo.rationale: Flat. The hike path is already in the strip and the foreign-exchange break has already printed, so new risk would be financed to join a move that is public.

funding_view.implication: Staying at the 3.92 official fixing beats paying that funding on new shocked-risk capital. The curve is already the price of the public hawkish news, so flat cash is a refusal to finance the chase, not a claim of alpha.
funding_view.sr3_forward_view: Implied secured funding is 4.30 in December 2026, 4.575 in March 2027, 4.71 in June, 4.735 in September, and 4.695 in December 2027, versus the 3.92 cash fixing.

no-trade-skeptic.invalidation: Leave cash only for a catalyst these marks have not already repriced, in an instrument whose expected move exceeds the funding cost of the risk capital. A further extension of the same breakdown does not qualify.
no-trade-skeptic.thesis: The book stays at cash. Secured funding is already 4.30 in December and 4.735 in September against a 3.92 fixing, and euro at 1.0968 has already broken. The hawkish minutes and the half-point remark are public. Paying funding on new risk to join that break is a post-catalyst chase.

rates_candidate.rationale: Entry 5.24 versus 5.07 is still a gain, but the five-day rise, the hawkish minutes, and September funding at 4.735 versus cash at 3.92 say the path is higher.

expression_memo.rationale: Close the 10-year long. The policy path is higher, equities have not broken, and euro at 1.0968 is a late dollar chase rather than a cleaner defensive expression.

perma-bear.invalidation: The close is wrong if September implied reverses toward cash at 3.92 and the 10-year falls away from 5.07 without reclaiming 5.24. A 10-year yield back through 5.24 confirms the close.
perma-bear.thesis: The 10-year long is closed. Yield is 5.07 versus a 5.24 entry, so the position is still ahead, but the five-day move is nine basis points against it and September secured funding at 4.735 sits about 80 basis points above cash at 3.92. The minutes lean hawkish, oil is an inflation impulse, and equities at 7323 have not broken, so this is not being paid as a slowdown hedge.

expression_memo.rationale: Close the 15 million Australian-dollar long. Spot 0.6731 versus 0.6757 is a 20-day downside break, and replacing it with another cyclical long would repurchase the same breakdown.
Close the September 2027 receive. Implied at 4.735 versus a 4.71 entry is the wrong side of a hike lean, and paying it after the rise would be a chase.

perma-bull.invalidation: The flat stance is wrong if the Australian dollar reclaims the broken range and copper firms, and if September implied falls back through 4.71 because the hike lean fades.

causal.assumptions_right: The front end could reprice higher without a growth collapse. Equities are still high and the U.S. minutes have leaned toward more hikes, which is consistent with a higher path.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The oil spike and the low-vol reading were overweighted. A plain hawkish shift in the reaction function was underweighted, and that is what lifted implied rates.
causal.causal_divergence: The short moved because expected policy rates rose. The oil-and-vol scenario used as the exit never arrived, so the written invalidation described a different regime from the live driver.
causal.future_implication: A later Australian front-end pay should be exited off the cash-rate path and the growth data. It should not be re-shorted just because 4.905 is above the old entry.
causal.observed_reality: Implied rose to 4.92 at the exit and is still 4.905. Brent is 91.95 and equity vol is 25.46, so the contract stayed higher without the spike-and-complacency regime that was written down.
causal.original_belief: March 2027 Australian overnight rates at 4.76 looked too low if growth held up. An oil spike and depressed equity volatility were treated as the conditions that would make the pay unsafe.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: Brent at 91.95 and equity vol at 25.46 did not meet the stated invalidation, and implied was still well above 4.76. The same information supported keeping the pay under a rate-path rule.

postmortems.future_rule: Cover a short March Australian overnight rate only if implied falls back through the entry because the hike lean fades, or if Australian growth breaks while front-end implied is already elevated.
postmortems.lesson: A front-end pay is invalidated by the policy path and by growth, not by a commodity extreme that is not the binding constraint.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: The belief that the Australian front end was too low versus a still-restrictive path was right. The regime filter attached to that belief described a different world from the one that repriced the contract.
postmortems.what_failed: The written invalidation was an oil spike and a low equity-vol reading. Brent is 91.95 and equity vol is 25.46, so the risk that was supposed to end the short never printed.
postmortems.what_worked: The March 2027 Australian overnight-rate short was the right direction. Implied rose from 4.76 at entry to 4.92 at the exit and is still 4.905.

causal.assumptions_right: Front-end funding could reprice higher without an equity break. The equity market still fits a growth tape that can live with a higher policy path.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The first two basis points were treated as enough of the move. How far a still-active hike lean could carry March, from 4.54 on to 4.575, was underweighted.
causal.causal_divergence: The direction matched the reaction function. The error was the exit clock: the cover happened while the same hike lean was still pushing the implied rate higher.
causal.future_implication: A future short in March secured funding needs a pre-committed path rule. It should not be chased at 4.575 merely to replace the early exit.
causal.observed_reality: Implied rose from 4.52 to 4.54 at the exit and now stands at 4.575. The minutes have leaned toward more hikes, and equities are still elevated.
causal.original_belief: March 2027 secured funding at 4.52 looked too low for an expansion that would keep policy restrictive. The pay was meant to work if growth stayed intact.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: At the exit the implied rate was only 4.54 against a 4.52 entry and restriction was not being walked back. The same information supported holding the pay.

postmortems.future_rule: Do not cover a short March 2027 secured-funding contract after a roughly two-basis-point rise while communication still leans toward more hikes. Keep it until implied reverses through the entry or the hike lean is walked back.
postmortems.lesson: A small rise in implied secured funding is not a reason to cover a pay while the central bank is still leaning toward more hikes and equities have not broken.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: Paying March because restriction would stick was a sound expression, and the later path confirmed it. The thesis held. The holding period did not.
postmortems.what_failed: The cover at 4.54 treated a two-basis-point rise as a completed move. The later lift to 4.575 showed the exit came before the hawkish communication was in the front end.
postmortems.what_worked: The March 2027 secured-funding short was the right pro-growth rates expression. Implied rose from 4.52 to 4.54 at the exit and has since reached 4.575.

perma-bull.thesis: Both cyclical legs come off. The Australian dollar at 0.6731 is through a 20-day low, with RSI at 23.4 and copper soft, so the long is the wrong pro-growth expression even with equities still high. September 2027 secured funding at 4.735 is above the 4.71 entry, and the minutes lean toward more hikes, so the receive is on the wrong side of the path. Nothing replaces them today.

expression_memo.rationale: Close the 10 million dollar-yen short. It is a stale level idea. Do not fade every fresh dollar break in the same breath.

spot_candidate.rationale: A high level without a breakout is not an ownership asymmetry. The price extremes sit in the other dollar pairs, and those are not being faded.

positioning-cynic.invalidation: The close is wrong if dollar-yen itself prints a 20-day upside break, which would be a real extension to fade, or if the fresh dollar-up breaks reverse while this short was still the open dollar-down leg.
positioning-cynic.thesis: The dollar-yen short is closed and nothing replaces it. Speculative positioning is not in the marks, so crowding can only be read from the price extreme, and that extreme is the fresh dollar-up complex in euro, sterling, the Australian dollar, the kiwi, dollar-Canada, and dollar-franc. Dollar-yen at 159.42 has a one-year z-score of 0.52 and no 20-day breakout, so the short has no stretched long to harvest. The 10-year up nine basis points is an impulse that usually carries dollar-yen higher.

rates_candidate.rationale: March at 3.00 to December at 3.325 still prices a 2027 re-steepening above a 2.83 terminal, while December funding remains near 2.795.

expression_memo.rationale: Hold the existing Canada 2027 curve receive. Do not add into the five-day selloff and do not open a U.S. receive because the Canada long is uncomfortable.

harvest_review.remaining_edge_reason: The Canada 2027 curve still prices a re-hike premium above a 2.83 terminal, and a fresh receive of that curve at the current strip would still be the underpriced easing. The five-day selloff is not a reason to add, and it is not a reason to abandon the existing receive.

reunderwrite.catalyst_logic: The edge is exhausted if the invalidation level in the thesis prints before the horizon.
reunderwrite.realization_logic: The position pays if the path described in the thesis is still the one in the marks.

rate-dove.invalidation: The hold dies if the Canada 2027 curve revisits the 3.4 entry, if December Canadian funding lifts through March at 3.00 and away from the 2.83 terminal, or if the Bank of Canada validates a hike path rather than scenarios.
rate-dove.thesis: The Canada 2027 curve long stays, and nothing is added. December Canadian funding at 2.795 already sits on a February terminal near 2.83, so further cuts are not the underpriced easing. The underpriced path is the re-hike premium from that terminal out to December 2027 at 3.325. The five-day selloff in Canada's two-year, up 17 basis points to 3.30, looks like U.S. spillover. A U.S. receive is not the replacement.

rates_candidate.rationale: September at 4.735 versus a 4.755 entry is the peak of a strip that already runs from cash at 3.92 through March at 4.575 and June at 4.71.

expression_memo.rationale: Cover the 12.5 million September short. The two-year has already repriced to 4.80 and September at 4.735 lagged that move.

rate-hawk.invalidation: The cover is wrong if September implied rises through the two-year at 4.80, which would mean the terminal peak is still being repriced and this contract is leading rather than lagging.

causal.assumptions_right: December hike pricing was too low, because implied rose from 4.12 to 4.30. The jobs and oil breaks did not arrive, so the short was not run over by an easing narrative.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The exit rule underweighted how completely a front contract can finish its repricing once the strip has climbed from 3.92 toward the mid-4s. It also underweighted that the two-year rose while September fell from 4.755 to 4.735.
causal.causal_divergence: The trade did not end on its stated invalidation. December moved because the policy path was marked toward more hikes, and the cover landed on a contract that has since sat near 4.30.
causal.future_implication: Harvest the front short when that contract has priced the path and fresh hawkish talk is being marked into the two-year. Keep the peak contract as a separate decision.
causal.observed_reality: The short was closed at 4.29 and December is now 4.30. There is no weak jobs report in the marks, and Brent at 91.95 with WTI at 83.26 is not oil breaking lower.
causal.original_belief: December 2026 secured funding at 4.12 underpriced further hikes. The short was to be dropped if a weak jobs report opened the door to easing or if oil broke lower.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same entry, the same jobs-or-oil invalidation, and the same path to 4.29, the short was the position to hold through that repricing. The marks do not show a second leg after the exit.

postmortems.future_rule: Cover a front secured-funding short when that contract has built the path and fresh hawkish communication is showing up in the two-year rather than in the contract. Do not roll the closed front short into the peak contract to keep the thesis alive.
postmortems.lesson: A short-rate short is finished when the contract that had room to price incremental hikes has built that path. A peak contract does not inherit the result just because the reaction function is still described as hawkish.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: The hawkish front-end thesis was confirmed. December rose from 4.12 into the 4.29 area and then stalled. The thesis was not invalidated. It reached the front contract and stopped.
postmortems.what_failed: The written invalidation was a weak jobs report or oil breaking lower, and neither caused the outcome. The exit rule did not say what to do when the front contract finished the hike repricing with oil still firm.
postmortems.what_worked: The December 2026 secured-funding short was the contract that actually repriced, from 4.12 to a cover at 4.29. December is now 4.30, and the jobs and oil invalidation never became the exit.

rate-hawk.thesis: The September 2027 secured-funding short is covered. The strip already peaks there at 4.735, only a couple of basis points above June, and the contract fell from the 4.755 entry while the two-year rose seven basis points to 4.80. The hawkish minutes have been marked into the front end. September is the priced peak, not an underpriced hike, and no new short is opened further along the strip.

rates_candidate.rationale: March at 4.575 versus cash at 3.92 is the working policy-path trend. September at 4.735 shows the strip is still higher further out.

expression_memo.rationale: Hold the 25 million March short. Entry 4.545 to 4.575 is with the move, and adding a euro short would duplicate a trend the policy contract already holds.

harvest_review.remaining_edge_reason: March implied at 4.575 versus a 4.545 entry is still with the hawkish trend, and a fresh short at this level would still be the policy-path continuation while the two-year is 4.80.

reunderwrite.catalyst_logic: The edge is exhausted if the invalidation level in the thesis prints before the horizon.
reunderwrite.realization_logic: The position pays if the path described in the thesis is still the one in the marks.

trend-follower.invalidation: Close the March short if implied is back below 4.53 and the U.S. two-year is back below 4.67. Until that prints, the hawkish repricing is the trend.

causal.assumptions_right: The hawkish lean and the higher-yield trend were the right backdrop. The two-year rose seven basis points to 4.80 and the 10-year rose nine to 5.07, so the rates confirmation remained in force through the close.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The exit treated a slow, non-breakout spot path as a completed trend. That overweighted the lack of a 20-day breakout and underweighted the written rule that the position stays open until the range or the rates stop.
causal.causal_divergence: The thesis and the rates confirmation kept pointing to holding the long. The close happened with those conditions still true, and spot later stood at 159.42 with the same invalidation unmet.
causal.future_implication: The March short stays because implied has risen from 4.545 to 4.575 and the 4.53 and 4.67 stop has not printed. Dollar-yen is not reopened while it is not a breakout and the working continuation is the short-rate position.
causal.observed_reality: The long was closed at 159.30. Spot is now 159.42, the two-year is 4.80, and March funding is 4.575, so neither written invalidation has printed. The pair is still not a 20-day breakout.
causal.original_belief: The dollar-yen long from 159.23 was a continuation of the hawkish U.S. rates trend. It was supposed to remain open until price fell back inside the prior range or the two-year fell below 4.67 and March funding fell below 4.53.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: At the close the two-year was not below 4.67, March funding was not below 4.53, and price had not fallen back inside the prior range. That same information would have kept the long open.

postmortems.future_rule: If a dollar-yen long is open, hold it until price falls back inside the prior range or until the two-year is below 4.67 and March secured funding is below 4.53. Do not close an open trend for lack of a new breakout.
postmortems.lesson: A trend position stays open until the written invalidation prints. Lack of a fresh breakout is a reason not to add, not an exit signal while the stated stops are unmet.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: The thesis was intact at the close and is intact now. The failure is the exit, which fired without a fall back inside the prior range and without the two-year below 4.67 and March below 4.53.
postmortems.what_failed: The long was closed at 159.30 while the written invalidation had not printed. Absence of a fresh breakout was used as an exit while the rates confirmation was still on the original side of the trade.
postmortems.what_worked: The hawkish backdrop stayed intact after the dollar-yen entry at 159.23. The two-year is 4.80, March secured funding is 4.575, and dollar-yen is 159.42 after the close at 159.30.

trend-follower.thesis: The March 2027 secured-funding short stays. Implied has moved from 4.545 to 4.575, with the trend, and the two-year at 4.80 and the 10-year at 5.07 are revising the same way. Euro at 1.0968 is a real downside break of the same impulse. The booked short is the cleaner continuation because the catalyst is the policy path. Dollar-yen is not the spot break and is not reopened.

expression_memo.rationale: Close the 5 million euro-sterling long. Fourteen pips of adverse mark is not the reason. The missing convergence trigger is.

spot_candidate.rationale: Spot 0.8329 versus 0.8343 is a one-year extreme that is also a fresh downside break, and the concurrent euro break means the cheap leg is still being sold.

value-guy.invalidation: The close is wrong if euro-sterling reclaims the pre-break 20-day range and trades back through the 0.8343 entry while euro stops extending its own downside break.
value-guy.thesis: The euro-sterling long is closed. A one-year percentile of 0.2 is a real dislocation, and the fresh 20-day break says that floor is still being left behind. Euro itself at 1.0968 is the stricter cheap leg and it is still breaking, so convergence has no start. Canada's two-year jump against Europe's 3.13 two-year is a dollar-bloc yield impulse, not a reason for this cross to mean-revert.

expression_memo.rationale: No premium is quoted, so nothing is bought or sold. Shorting the dollar break in spot would be the linear risk this seat is here to challenge.

vol-convexity.invalidation: This flat stance ends only when a later set of marks quotes an actual premium, strike, and tenor. A further extension of the same spot breaks does not create the option.
vol-convexity.thesis: The book stays flat. Equity vol is 25.46 and several dollar pairs are through their 20-day ranges, but the marks contain no option premium, no strike, and no tenor. Those spot breaks are linear risk with an uncapped gap. They are not a substitute for an option that cannot be priced.

deployment_hurdle.benchmark: The zero-alpha benchmark is the 3.92 cash secured-funding fixing. Expected edge must clear that fixing on shocked risk capital.

ignored_unrelated_gaps: New Zealand sovereign yields are research-only and this spot does not need them.
candidate_assessments.rationale: Spot 1.0968 is already through the break and the dollar seat still holds the short. A new short reopens a completed expression. Neither a new short nor a fade has expected edge above 3.92.

ignored_unrelated_gaps: New Zealand sovereign yields are research-only and are not this contract.
candidate_assessments.rationale: The strip already prices hikes versus 3.92 cash. Receiving works only if that path is not delivered. Paying buys a path that is already priced and already held.

ignored_unrelated_gaps: New Zealand sovereign yields are research-only and this spot does not need them.
candidate_assessments.rationale: The Australian dollar at 0.6731 has already broken. Shorting it reopens a completed expression, and buying it fades a stretch that was closed rather than faded.

deployment_hurdle.chosen_action_rationale: Euro, the Australian dollar, and March secured funding are markable and all fail the hurdle. The crosses are finished breaks, and March is already the hike story. Flat cash takes no shocked-risk funding charge.

grinder.invalidation: A markable dislocation whose expected edge on shocked risk exceeds the 3.92 fixing, that does not reopen a cross already through its extreme, and that does not depend on the hike path failing to arrive.

opportunity_scan.rationale: The euro short is already held and 1.0968 is through the break. Reopening it repeats a completed expression.
0.6731 has already broken. The completed-break rule bars a fresh Australian-dollar short.
Paying March buys a hike path that is already in the price and already held. Receiving it bets that the minutes are wrong.

grinder.thesis: Stay flat. Euro at 1.0968 and the Australian dollar at 0.6731 have already broken, so those expressions are complete. The secured-funding strip from 4.30 to 4.735 already is the hike path, so March neither pays an unpriced edge above the 3.92 fixing nor deserves new risk.

pragmatist.invalidation: The flat stance is wrong if dollar-yen completes a breakout while euro holds 1.0968 and dollar-franc holds 0.8427, or if a new Canada anchor appears that is separate from the finished March sleeve.

opportunity_scan.rationale: Downside break at 1.0968 is already held by the dollar seat. The failure level is not clean enough to add a second copy.
March at 4.575 versus cash at 3.92 is a path that is already marked, and the trend seat already holds the short.
The receive from 3.13 was flattened at 2.96. The live mark at 3.00 is a bounce in a finished sleeve.

portfolio_construction.adverse_scenario: The adverse path for a flat book is opportunity cost: euro extends the break through 1.0968, dollar-franc extends through 0.8427, and March secured funding rises further from 4.575, while cash still earns only the 3.92 fixing.

candidate_interactions.rationale: A new euro short would duplicate the dollar-seat hold of the same downside break.
A new March pay would duplicate the trend seat's working short after the path is already in the price.
Reloading the finished Canadian residual does not complement a flat book.

portfolio_construction.chosen_actions_rationale: Stay flat. The personal Canada sleeve is complete, and the live dollar and front-end expressions are already held elsewhere. Equity vol at 25.46 keeps preservation ahead of a second copy.
portfolio_construction.existing_book_summary: The book is flat. The March 2027 Canadian funding receive was closed at 2.96 after a 3.13 entry, and cash is the zero benchmark at the 3.92 secured-funding fixing.

rejected_complements.reason: The downside break is real and already held. A second copy does not change the factor.
The upside break duplicates the same dollar beta.
The Australian dollar break was closed this round, and firm crude fights that commodity leg.
March at 4.575 already prices a wide gap to cash at 3.92 and is already held.
The residual completed at 2.96 and is not reloaded at 3.00.

causal.assumptions_right: The residual did travel from 3.13 to 2.96 in the expected direction. Closing the full sleeve at the anchor released the risk rather than leaving a stub through the bounce.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The outright was the whole expression, so once the two-year repriced there was no remaining curve leg to adjust. That single-point shape was underweighted relative to the later front-end selloff.
causal.causal_divergence: The flatten was driven by anchor completion, not by the hike reaction that had been written as the invalidation. The sleeve ended because the residual was done, while the two-year move arrived afterward.
causal.future_implication: The sleeve stays flat at a 3.00 mark after a 2.96 exit until a new anchor and a new invalidation are written. Copying someone else's Canada curve long would reopen the finished residual.
causal.observed_reality: The receive was flattened at 2.96. The contract now marks 3.00, and the Canada two-year is 3.30 after a 17 basis point rise in five days. The hike invalidation had not printed at the exit.
causal.original_belief: The March 2027 Canadian funding receive was a residual compression from 3.13 toward its anchor, with the February terminal near 2.83 as the distant reference. A Bank of Canada hike or a front-strip move into the 2027 mid-3s was the invalidation.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: At 2.96 the residual had reached the anchor and the hike path was not yet the driver. The same information supported a full flatten rather than a reshape of a finished point.

postmortems.future_rule: A finished anchor closes the sleeve. March 2027 Canadian funding at 3.00 after an exit at 2.96 stays untouched until a new anchor and a new invalidation are written down.
postmortems.lesson: When a relative-value residual has completed at its anchor, flatten it and do not reload the finished sleeve.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: The path from 3.13 to 2.96 realized the residual, and the live mark at 3.00 is a bounce in a finished sleeve rather than a new anchor.
postmortems.what_failed: The expression was a single March 2027 point, so once the two-year repriced to 3.30 the finished outright had no remaining curve leg to adjust.
postmortems.what_worked: The receive from 3.13 harvested the move to 2.96, and the full flatten at the anchor kept the sleeve from sitting through the bounce to 3.00 and the Canada two-year selloff.

pragmatist.thesis: The book stays flat. The March Canadian funding receive already completed from 3.13 to 2.96 and is not reloaded at 3.00. The dollar breaks are real, and yen is not confirming them. March secured funding at 4.575 already sits far above cash at 3.92. With equity vol at 25.46, preservation beats a second copy of risks the desk already holds.

lifecycle.catalyst_logic: The catalyst is the hawkish minutes and the half-point remark. If the break cannot extend after that communication, the catalyst has been spent.
lifecycle.realization_logic: The short pays if the 20-day downside break extends while dollar-franc and the Australian dollar keep the dollar bid.

swinger.invalidation: Close the euro short if euro trades back through 1.1120, or if the policy communication before December 4 clearly reverses the hawkish lean.

opportunity_scan.rationale: Cleanest liquid expression of the hawkish dollar bid, already through a 20-day downside break at 1.0968.
Upside break at 0.8427 confirms the same dollar bid and is the spare expression if the euro break fails.
A pay at 4.575 would reload the short covered at 4.54. That stalled decline is not reopened.

causal.assumptions_right: Keeping 4.40 as the falsification level was right, because the selloff exhausted above it. The assumption that hawkish communication could put a floor under funding was also right, given the bounce to 4.575.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The decision underweighted the invalidation and treated the decline itself as enough to exit. The 4.62 entry also underweighted how far the hawkish outcome was already priced, which left no cushion when the contract backed up.
causal.causal_divergence: The thesis called for a higher March rate unless 4.40 broke, but the book was flat by the time the rate turned back up. The gap is the cover at 4.54, not a later fact that overturned the policy path.
causal.future_implication: This round trip does not authorize a new receive, because that decline has already stalled. It also does not authorize buying back the same March short at 4.575. The next risk is a different expression of the hawkish dollar path.
causal.observed_reality: The mark fell to 4.54 and the short was closed there, well above the 4.40 invalidation. March is now 4.575, the decline has stalled, and the newest minutes leaned hawkish.
causal.original_belief: March 2027 secured funding was shorted at 4.62 on the view that the policy path would keep the implied rate rising. The position was to be held until that view paid or until a fall to 4.40 showed the hawkish path had been priced out.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: Using only the entry, the 4.40 invalidation, and the path through 4.54, the short should have remained open. Held to 4.575, the gap versus 4.62 would have been smaller than the loss that was realized.

postmortems.future_rule: Do not cover a secured-funding short before the written invalidation unless the catalyst itself has flipped, and do not immediately re-open that same short as a new ticket.
postmortems.lesson: Covering a short solely because price has fallen, while the written invalidation still holds, converts an open drawdown into a realized loss at the stall. A finished decline is also not a signal to reload the same short.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: The pay thesis was bruised by an early entry and was not wrong in direction once the dip stalled. It was abandoned inside the invalidation band, not killed by the market.
postmortems.what_failed: The short entered at 4.62 was covered at 4.54, while the kill level at 4.40 was still unhit. The cover sat on the stall, so the bounce back to 4.575 and the hawkish minutes arrived with the book already flat.
postmortems.what_worked: The written invalidation at 4.40 correctly marked where the hawkish funding view would have been falsified, and March never traded there. After the cover, the contract recovered from 4.54 to 4.575, so the dip stalled rather than extending into a thesis break.

swinger.thesis: The swing is a concentrated euro short. Euro at 1.0968 is through the 20-day low after hawkish minutes, dollar-franc and the Australian dollar confirm the dollar bid, and dollar-yen at 159.42 is not the break. The March funding short that was covered at 4.54 is not reopened, and the euro is a different expression of the same hawkish dollar path.
